newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle $69, light volume - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle $69, light volume - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $69.00 per cwt in light activity, steady with this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head of steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, the sources said.
Friday's light sales follow a weekly movement of 118,100 head, USDA said. Kansas weekly sales were pegged 95,500 head.
Feedlot cattle next week were expected to be priced by owners at $71.00 to $72.00 amid expectations for continued strong beef prices and tight finished cattle supplies.
Beef prices have been supported by strong domestic demand, said Dale Benson, livestock analyst with Dean Witter Reynolds.

Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.53 to $1.02 per cwt, with 163 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. The heavier weight choice beef was up $0.68 at $106.64, up $7.19 from last Friday's close, USDA statistics showed.

Showlists next week were expected smaller and holding an increased percentage of "green" or unfinished cattle following strong sales the past three weeks which have left many feedlots extremely current.
